DILG Republic of the Philippines IENT OF INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT enter, EDSA comer Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City www.dilq.qov.ph DILG OPINION No. 114 s. 2021 17 September 2021 Ms. ELLA G. MONDIDON eegmondi@gmail.com Dear Ms. Mondidon: This refers to your electronic mail dated 02 June 2021 requesting that the Department conducts an investigation on the Certificate of Indigency issued by Barangay Caridad, Bago City, Negros Occidental to a certain Mr. Jose Rey Muchada Mondidon (Jose Rey) who, you claims, is not a person of indigent status. You further stated that Jose Rey used the Certificate of Indigency to avail of free legal services from the Public Attorney's Office (PAO). You stated that Jose Rey should have been disqualified from being issued a Certificate of Indigency because: (a) he is the owner of a bakery; (b) his household in Barangay Alijis, Bacolod City is newly built; and (c) he has been driving an Isuzu Crosswind for the past five (5) years. You credit the issuance of the Certificate of Indigency to his mother, Ms. Fe Machuda Mondidon (Fe), who is allegedly a Sangguniang Member of Barangay Caridad. You, however, admitted that the house could be owned by Fe. You further stated that John Rey has three (3) sisters who are all Overseas Filipino Workers, and that they may own the Isuzu Crosswind. This Department respectfully manifests that, pursuant to its power of general supervision, it can only see to it that a local government unit is compliant with existing laws. This Department has no authority to annul the actions of a local government unit absent a law to the contrary. Presently, there is no provision of law setting the minimum standards for the issuance of a Certificate of Indigency by a barangay. As per the principle of local autonomy, the same is, therefore, subject to the discretion of the barangay as may be provided by their local ordinance. Additionally, barangay officials enjoy the presumption of regularity in the performance of their duties. The principle was aptly explained by the Supreme Court in the case of Empaynado vs. Court of Appeals (G.R. No. 91606, 17 December 1991), which states: "Moreover, the presumption that the Barangay Captain has regularly performed his official duty has not been rebutted by any convincing and substantial evidence... The private respondents failed to refute the aforequoted statements. Their verbal assertions casting doubt on the disputed certification "Matino, Mahusay at Maasahan" Trunkline No.: 8876-34-54

remain just that. Belief, suspicion and conjectures cannot overcome the presumption of regularity and legality which attaches to the disputed certification. Hence, in the absence of contrary evidence, it is presumed that everything done by the Barangay Captain in connection with the issuance of the disputed certification was done pursuant to law. " The alleged Certificate of Indigency is therefore presumed to have been issued in compliance with applicable laws, unless clear and convincing evidence states the contrary. Presently, we regret to inform you that you have failed to submit copies the local ordinance stating the qualifications by which Barangay Caridad shall issue the certificate, and proof pertaining to the non-compliance thereto. A copy of the alleged Certificate of Indigency was not even attached to the electronic mail. You bare allegations, unfortunately, do not constitute sufficient proof which may be used by this Department to overturn an alleged action of a local government unit. Regardless, in case Jose Rey was indeed represented by PAO in a legal matter, please be assured that PAO requires, aside from the subject barangay certificate, the latest Income Tax Return and a Certificate of Indigency from the Department of Social Welfare and Development, or it local counterpart. In other words, PAO would not have represented John Rey had he failed to prove his indigent status. This opinion is being rendered without prejudice to any contrary opinion of competent authorities and the courts. Thank you. Very tr ours, Y AUTHORITY OF THE SEC ETARY: ARTI B.
